articles.text: NÁNPÉNGYOU: Xiǎo Lán, jīntian wǒ bàba zài jiā, wǎnshang dào wǒmen jiā chī fàn ba!
BOYFRIEND: Xiǎo Lán, my father is home today; why don't you have dinner at our house tonight?
XIǍO LÁN: Wǒ bú qù.
XIǍO LÁN: I'm not going.
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Wèishénme? Wǒ bàba rén hěn hǎo, nǐ bú bì dānxīn.
BOYFRIEND: Why? My father's a very good person — you don't have to worry.
XIǍO LÁN: Wǒ mā shuō...
XIǍO LÁN: My mother said...
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Nǐ mā shuō shénme?
BOYFRIEND: What did your mother say?
XIǍO LÁN: Wǒ mā shuō: nǐ jiā rén duō, nǐ yéye, nǎinai hái zài, xiōngdì jiěmèi nàjǐge, jiāli guīju yě bù shǎo, pà wǒ qùle yǐhòu chī kǔ.

XIǍO LÁN: My mother said that you have a big family. Your grandparents are still alive, you have so many brothers and sisters, and your family has such a strict code of behavior, that she was afraid I would have a rough time after I went.
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Hài, nǐ xiǎngde tài duō le. Wǒ nǎinai guòqù zuò érxífude shíhou chīguo hěn duō kǔ, suǒyǐ tā duì wǒ māma tèbié hǎo. Nǐ xiǎng wǒ nǎinai, wǒ māma tāmen zěnme huì ràng nǐ chī kǔ ne?

BOYFRIEND: Oh come on, you're thinking too much. Back when my grandmother was a daughter-in-law she had quite a rough time, so she's particularly good to my mother. Really, how could my grandmother and mother give you a hard time!
XIǍO LÁN: Xiànzài dāngrán hái hǎo, yǐhòu ne? Yídàjiā rén zhù zài yíkuàir, shíjiān chángle zǒng shi hěn máfande.
XIǍO LÁN: Of course it's okay now, but how about later on? When a large family lives together, it always gets difficult after a while.
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Zhèi yìdiǎn wǒ yě xiǎngdàole. Niánji dàle, xiǎngfǎ yǒude shíhou hé niánqīng rén bú tài yíyàng. Yǐhòu yǒule fángzi wǒmen bānchūlai jiù xíng le.

BOYFRIEND: I've thought of that too. When people get older, their way of thinking is sometimes kind of different from young people. Afterwards when we get a place of our own we'll move out, and then it will be all right.
XIǍO LÁN: Shénme shíhour cái néng yǒu fángzi ne?
XIǍO LÁN: And when will we be able to get a place to live?
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Bié jí, wǒ xiǎng bú huì děng hěn cháng shíjiānde.
BOYFRIEND: Don't worry, I don't think we'll have to wait too long.
XIǍO LÁN: Èng.
XIǍO LÁN: Mm.
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Nàme, jīntian wǎnshang dào wǒmen jiā qu, hǎo ma?
BOYFRIEND: Then, how about going to our house tonight?
XIǍO LÁN: Mm... Jīntian wǎnshang dōu yǒu shéi?
XIǍO LÁN: Mm... Who's going to be there tonight?
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Zhǐ yǒu wǒ bàba, māma, hé wǒ. Xiōngdì jiěmèi dōu bú zài.
BOYFRIEND: Just my father, mother, and I. None of my brothers and sisters will be there.
XIǍO LÁN: Nà, yéye, nǎinai ne?
XIǍO LÁN: What about your grandparents?
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Yéye nǎinai hē cháde shíhou guòlai zuò yíxiàr, ránhòu jiù huí tāmen wūzi xiūxi qu le.
BOYFRIEND: They'll come out and sit for a while when we have tea, and then they'll go back to their room to rest.
XIǍO LÁN: Tóuyícì qù, wǒ dài diǎnr shénme hǎo a?
XIǍO LÁN: What should I bring, since this is my first visit?
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Shénme dōu bú yào dài.
BOYFRIEND: Don't bring anything at all.
XIǍO LÁN: Nà zěnme xíng? Tīngshuō nǐ yéyede zì xiěde hěn hǎo a?
XIǍO LÁN: How can I do that? I hear your grandfather is very good at writing characters?
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Shì a, zěnme la?
BOYFRIEND: That's right. Why?
XIǍO LÁN: Wǒ bàba yǒu yítào shǒuchāode Sì Shū, sòng gěi nǐ yéye hǎo bu hǎo?
XIǍO LÁN: My father has a handwritten copy of the Four Books. How about if I give it to your grandfather?
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Nà tài hǎo le.
BOYFRIEND: That would be great.
XIǍO LÁN: Wǒ huí jiā shōushi yíxiàr jiù lái.
XIǍO LÁN: I'm going to go home now to straighten up a bit and then I'll be right there.
NÁNPÉNGYOU: Děng yìhuǐr wǒ lái jiē ni a!
BOYFRIEND: I'll come and get you in a while!
XIǍO LÁN: Ēi!
XIǍO LÁN: Okay!
